rationale: unreadable

Clause 10(c) excludes Erchonia's liability for loss of profit and consequential damages including claims from product defects, while clause 11(a) promises indemnity for third-party IP and legal non-compliance claims without being made subject to or carved out from that exclusion.
suggested_fix: Add to clause 10(c): 'except for Erchonia's indemnification obligations under Section 11(a), which shall not be limited by this Section.'

rationale: Clause 8 vests all IP in the Products in Erchonia while clause 9(a) separately reserves Trademarks, including 'Product design' and packaging design, so Product design is governed by both with differing treatment.
suggested_fix: Clarify in 9(a) that Product design is governed by Section 8 for ownership and by Section 9 only for the licensed trademark use.

rationale: unreadable

Section 10.4 Program Transfer is conditioned on payment of 'all amounts due' and funding the Termination Reserve Account, which depend on the settlement and payment mechanics, including ISO's top-up duty 'upon demand', in section 6.2.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer in 10.4(a) to the amounts determined under Section 6.2 and state the period within which they must be quantified and paid.

rationale: Section 12.3 consequences of termination and expiry operate alongside the non-refundable upfront payment in 9.1, whose treatment on termination is not stated in 12.3.
suggested_fix: State in 12.3 that the upfront payment under Section 9.1 remains non-refundable on any termination.

rationale: Suspension in 10(a) is barred pending resolution of payment disputes 'pursuant to Section 19', so its operation depends on the arbitration clause, while termination rights in 10(b) run alongside the Ehave warranties in Section 14.
suggested_fix: State expressly that the five Business Day payment period after a Section 19 determination also applies to the 10(b) cure period and that warranty breach under Section 14 is a material breach.

rationale: The Up-Front Fee is payable on execution, but clause 4.2 is silent on whether it is refundable if the Term is terminated for Snap's breach, leaving the outcome for a court under s.73.
suggested_fix: Add that on termination for Snap's breach the unearned portion of the Up-Front Fee shall be refunded pro rata.

rationale: The right of first refusal in 4.4 operates only on expiry or termination of the Term fixed by 4.1 (December 31, 2000) and the 45-day notice is measured from that date.
suggested_fix: State that the 45-day notice period in 4.4 is calculated from the expiry date in Section 4.1 or from the date of any termination notice.

rationale: Section 6 of the Amendment removes the Section 13.1 liability limitation for Licensor's obligation to repay Royalty Advances under Section 3.2, but Section 3.2 as shown contains no express repayment mechanism, so the carve-out refers to an obligation that may not exist.
suggested_fix: Add to Section 3.2 an express obligation on Licensor to refund unrecouped Royalty Advances on termination or expiry within 30 days.

rationale: The six-month term auto-renews unless notice is given at least six months before the end of the then-current term, which is the entire length of the term, so non-renewal notice would have to be given on the first day or earlier and the right is effectively illusory.
suggested_fix: Reduce the non-renewal notice period in 2.01 to 30 days before the end of the then-current term.

rationale: Section 8.02 makes the payment of all monies due on termination 'subject to Section 4.03', which lets Contractor retain collections for 24 months after termination, so the payment obligation on exit is modified by the retention right.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer in 8.02 to the Withholding Period and cap the retained amount at a documented estimate with periodic statements to the Company.

rationale: Section 10.3 states what continues after termination (payment, liability for prior breach), while the obligations in clause 2 such as privacy are not stated to survive, so their post-termination effect depends on the survival wording.
suggested_fix: Add that VOTOCAST's privacy obligations in Section 2.1 survive termination for as long as it holds Licensee data.

rationale: The force majeure clause excludes 'payment obligations' from relief, so it works through the payment clause in Section 3, which carries 30-day terms and 1.5% monthly late interest.
The Minimum Revenue Targets for years 1 and 2 only take effect through the Term and termination clause, which sets a three-year Term and termination rights tied to performance.
suggested_fix: State expressly in Section 6(b) whether failure to meet the Minimum Revenue Targets is a material breach giving a right to terminate.

rationale: Section 3.2 makes all Proceeds Purchaser's property held in trust by Merchant, while Section 3.3 gives Agent sole control of Agency Accounts and Designated Deposit Accounts, so both govern custody of the same proceeds.
suggested_fix: Add that proceeds in the Agency Accounts are held subject to Section 3.2(b) trust and set out the order of application.

rationale: Section 8.10 makes Agent's use of the E-Commerce Platform subject to the Wind-Down Budget and to Expenses under Section 4.1(p), which Section 4.1 declares outside the Wind-Down Cap.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 8.10 that Section 4.1(p) Expenses are payable outside the Wind-Down Budget and Wind-Down Cap.

rationale: Section 4.4 returns Confidential Information on termination, while Section 9.1.1 requires confidentiality to continue 'for an indefinite period' afterwards, so which obligations survive termination turns on both clauses.
suggested_fix: Add that Sections 9.1 and 4.4 survive termination and that any retained copies remain subject to confidentiality for a defined period.

rationale: Clause 1.1.4 allows Vendor to terminate on change of control, and the payment of Monthly Compensation for up to 24 months under 1.6.2 is triggered by that termination, so the two work together.
suggested_fix: State that the post-termination Monthly Compensation is a genuine pre-estimate of loss and the sole remedy for change-of-control termination.

rationale: Clause 1.5 reverts the exclusive distribution right to Vendor on any termination, and the Section 8.4.1 reimbursement of return freight operates only on that termination.
suggested_fix: Clarify in 8.4.1 that the reimbursement obligation survives termination and state the cases in which it applies.

rationale: The stub-quarter fee in Clause A depends on termination of the Participation Agreement, which under Clause B also terminates this Agreement 'immediately and automatically', so fee entitlement rests on the termination mechanics and the 'misconduct' carve-out.
suggested_fix: Add to Section 4 that accrued fees under Section 3 for the stub quarter survive automatic termination and define 'misconduct' by reference to a final determination.

rationale: unreadable
Clause B lets Emerald elect the effective date within 30 days of the Contractor's notice, leaving unclear whether the fixed 24-month term in 5.1 or the 30-day window governs when obligations end.
suggested_fix: State that termination takes effect on the date specified by Emerald, not later than 30 days after notice, and that the Term ends on that date.

rationale: Warranty 19(a)(i) requires conformity to 'the specifications set forth in Section 1', but Section 1 only defines Terpene Product by reference to Exhibit A, so the warranty works only through that cross-reference.
suggested_fix: Amend 19(a)(i) to read 'conform to the specifications set forth in Exhibit A'.

rationale: The post-termination bar on using the Duval Identification in Section 12 interacts with Section 4 fees and refund of unearned Additional License Fee, which must be settled on termination.
suggested_fix: Add that on termination unearned Additional License Fee is refunded within a stated period and Section 12 use restrictions apply thereafter.

rationale: Section 16 termination on 30 days' notice does not say whether the unearned $375,000 Additional License Fee advance or prepaid Annual Fee under Section 4 is refundable or pro-rated.
suggested_fix: Add to Section 16 that on termination Licensor refunds the unearned portion of prepaid fees and the Additional License Fee within 30 days.

rationale: Section 5 adds earned remuneration to the Annual Fee for 'each remaining Contract Year', but Section 16 termination does not state how such escalated fees stop or are treated after termination.
suggested_fix: Provide that no additional remuneration or escalated Annual Fee accrues after the effective date of termination under Section 16.

rationale: The suspension limit in 10(a) depends on dispute resolution under Section 19, and escrow release in Section 12 is a related remedy on termination, so meaning relies on cross-references.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer in Section 10 to the Section 12(b) escrow release events upon termination for Ehave default.

rationale: Escrow in Section 12 must be in place by launch of the Companion Solution, which is a milestone defined in the Section 3 Implementation Plan.
suggested_fix: Specify the escrow deposit deadline by reference to a defined milestone in the Implementation Plan.

rationale: The Agent's obligation to 'immediately cease all use of the Trademarks' on expiration or termination operates only through the termination mechanics in Clause 4.
suggested_fix: Add to Clause 4 that Paragraph 3.2 (cessation of Trademark use) survives expiration or termination.

rationale: Termination clause 10.B gives ESSI a 10-day payment grace period yet also allows termination only after a further 3-day notice cure, and says Talent's termination does not relieve ESSI of consideration while 10.A relieves ESSI of all consideration on its own termination, creating inconsistent cure and payment outcomes tied to the Grant's Paragraph 3 rights.
suggested_fix: Align cure periods in Paragraph 10 and state expressly which consideration accrues and which Talent Attribute usage rights in Paragraph 3 end upon termination.

rationale: The Paragraph 3 grant of use of Talent Attributes is the performance for which the Paragraph 5 equity and cash consideration is paid, so the payment only works through the grant and Social Communication schedule.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer Paragraph 5 payments expressly to delivery of the Paragraph 3 grant and Social Communication services.

rationale: The table of contents lists Section 17.3.3 (consequences of Roche's termination for FMI breach), which is the operative clause that gives content to the termination structure in 17.2.

Survival clause 7.5 lists Section 9 as surviving, yet Section 9.4 lets Recipient retain a confidential copy only 'after termination or expiration', so duplicated survival and retention terms may be inconsistent with the return obligation.
Section 12 publicity restrictions continue after termination only because Survival clause 7.5 expressly lists Section 12.

Section 6.3 deems a Latent Defect lot rejected and applies Section 6.2, so the Latent Defect remedy works only through the 6.2 rejection and replacement procedure, whose acceptance deeming could conflict with later-discovered defects.
suggested_fix: State that deemed acceptance under 6.2(a) does not bar rejection of Latent Defects under 6.3.

rationale: Termination clause allows termination for any default or a 30-day unremedied breach (two thresholds), while Article 9 exclusivity on qualified opportunities is expressed to survive and 'no exclusivity otherwise', leaving inconsistent exit and exclusivity outcomes.
suggested_fix: Delete the bare 'in default' trigger and keep a single 30-day cure standard, and state whether exclusivity on qualified opportunities survives termination.

rationale: Section 7.4 preserves accrued liability on licence termination while warranties 8.11-8.12 assert no loss of rights and free transferability, so the warranty liability and the licence-termination carve-out may be differently scoped.

Clause 13 gives exclusive venue to the King County Superior Court or W.D. Washington courts, while Clause 15 sends any controversy to AAA arbitration in Seattle at any party's request, so the forum is contradictory.
suggested_fix: Make the court venue in Clause 13 expressly subject to Clause 15 and limit it to enforcement of awards and interim relief.

rationale: Clause 1 amends the Territory in Section 2 to add a region, and the exclusivity in Clause 2 operates only within that redacted territory and refers to an Exhibit 4a Marketing Plan that is yet to be agreed.
suggested_fix: Attach Exhibit 4a at signing and state that exclusivity applies only to the Territory as amended in Section 2.

rationale: Clause 5 caps the Sponsor's obligation at the fee but Racing's indemnity covers only loss 'in excess of the Maximum Obligation', and Clause 14 termination leaves the 'remaining provisions' in force, so the cap and indemnity interact unclearly after termination.
suggested_fix: Clarify that the indemnity applies to all losses including those within the Maximum Obligation and survives termination under Section 14.

rationale: Clause 3 says no payments are due after termination and Clause 9 gives a pro rata refund of fees paid on termination for conduct, so refund and payment cessation on termination are dealt with in differing terms.
suggested_fix: Add to Section 3 that on any termination, including under Section 9, fees are refunded pro rata for unperformed races.

rationale: Clause 3.2 fixes a 36-month minimum fee with a two-month suspension right, while Clause 3.3 allows stopping fees after 36 months only on deactivation and requires restart on reactivation, so duration and suspension terms overlap and may be inconsistent.
suggested_fix: Merge into one clause stating whether the suspension months count toward the 36-month minimum and the exact stop and restart conditions.

rationale: Clause 6(a) starts the 30-business-day acceptance period only after installation under Section 4 and training under Section 5, so acceptance depends on completion of those clauses.
suggested_fix: State that the acceptance period starts only on written confirmation that training under Section 5 is complete.

rationale: Clause 5.4.3 requires return of Confidential Information on termination, which operates through the Section 7 definition and exclusions, and 6.2 force majeure termination triggers that return obligation.
suggested_fix: Add that return/destruction under 5.4.3 is subject to the exclusions in Section 7.2 and that Section 7 obligations survive termination, including under Section 6.2.

rationale: Clause 2.3 sets payment terms and 1.5% monthly interest while 2.4 makes amounts tax-inclusive, so it is unclear whether late interest and invoiced amounts include taxes.
suggested_fix: Clarify that interest under 2.3 accrues only on undisputed amounts and that the tax-inclusive price in 2.4 is the base for invoicing.

rationale: Clause 2.1(b) says the Services Fee is full consideration except 'pursuant to Section 1.4', which makes Non-Covered Services billable under Section 2.2, and the emergency work without approval leaves the pricing basis dependent on the cross-reference.
suggested_fix: State that Non-Covered Services are billed at the Section 2.2 rates and require written Owner approval above $500 except in genuine emergencies.

rationale: unreadable

The operation clause makes Party A responsible for operation with the fee tied to generation, while the later clause makes Party A compensate Party B's 'actual loss' for outages or maintenance, so fee shortfall and compensation for the same underperformance may be duplicated with no cap.
suggested_fix: Define compensable 'actual loss', exclude indirect loss, and cap Party A's aggregate compensation, stating it is the sole remedy for the shortfall.

rationale: The fee is payable on completion and passing the grid-connection evaluation, but the start date is fixed at 72 hours of design-standard operation, and the 20-year term is cut off by a clause about equipment stopping, leaving the trigger and term unclear.
suggested_fix: Use a single defined commencement date (successful 72-hour run and grid connection) for fee liability and term, and state the consequences of equipment failure.

rationale: Clause 3.5 payments of Proceeds depend on the Proceeds sharing defined in 3.3 and the roles in Section 3, which is only an introductory heading.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer expressly to Section 3.3 for the Proceeds calculation and state the payment dates.

rationale: Clause 2.2 allows either party to terminate if no SOW is agreed within 2 months, while 2.3 allows termination if the Launch Date has not occurred within 4 months, giving two overlapping termination triggers for the same development delay.
suggested_fix: Clarify that the 2.2 right applies only to SOW agreement and the 2.3 right to launch delay, with a single notice procedure and no termination by a party at fault.

rationale: Clause 8.1 sets the term as one year from the Launch Date, yet 2.2 allows termination at 2 months and 8.1's renewal language both requires mutual written agreement and automatically renews absent notice.
suggested_fix: Restate 8.1 so renewal is either by mutual written agreement or automatic unless notice is given, not both, and make it expressly subject to Section 2.2 termination.

rationale: The royalty on Endorsed Products sold in Australia and New Zealand depends on the exclusive worldwide license in Paragraph 3 and the Contract Period definitions.

The Contract Period ends 31 December 1998 'unless sooner terminated', while clause 21 says termination does not relieve TPC of paying 'all compensation contemplated hereunder', leaving unclear whether that means the full remaining period's compensation, which risks being a penalty.
suggested_fix: Limit post-termination payment to sums accrued to the termination date plus reasonable pre-estimated damages, and state that notice and cure periods are under 21(b).

rationale: Clause 12(a) vests all marks in Fox and ends Licensee's rights on termination, while 13(a)(iv) infringement warranty covers Licensee Materials that must carry Fox notices, so the IP split depends on the definitions of Licensee Materials and Fox IP.
suggested_fix: Clarify that the 13(a)(iv) warranty excludes Fox Intellectual Property and PSM Materials supplied by Fox.

rationale: Clause 11(b) gives Fox ownership of all derivative works of the Properties, while clause 2(a) makes Licensee responsible for creating code and visual assets, so ownership of Licensee-created materials is addressed in two places with differing scope.
suggested_fix: State in clause 2(a) that deliverables created under it are subject to Fox's ownership under 11(b), with a written assignment in line with Copyright Act s.19.

rationale: The infringement warranty in 13(a)(iv) is the trigger for the indemnity in 14(a)(ii) for any breach of warranty, so the indemnity's scope depends on how wide the warranty is.
suggested_fix: Cap or qualify the 14(a)(ii) indemnity for breach of warranty and align it with the remedies in 13(a)(iv).

rationale: Section 10.3 post-termination obligations depend on the term and termination triggers in 10.1 and 10.2, and 10.2 is itself made subject to section 13.2.

Clause 6.1 compels Telnet to buy all devices from Galaxy, while clause 9.2 says nothing in the agreement licenses Trademarked Material even though Products carry Galaxy marks and Telnet may hold itself out as authorized seller, leaving the scope of permitted mark use unclear.
suggested_fix: Add a limited non-exclusive licence to use the Trademarked Material for marketing and resale of Products.

rationale: Section 10.2 lets either party terminate for material breach, but 8.3 bars any compensation or damages in connection with termination, including loss of investment, which can silently defeat claims arising from a wrongful termination.
suggested_fix: Clarify in 8.3 that it does not bar damages for accrued breaches before termination or for wrongful termination.

rationale: Galaxy's one-sided cap in 8.2 (liability limited to the Product purchase price) sits alongside Telnet's obligation in 6.1 to purchase all devices from Galaxy, leaving Telnet with limited remedy for a defective or undelivered Product it cannot source elsewhere.
suggested_fix: Make the 8.2 cap mutual and exclude fraud, wilful default and gross negligence.

rationale: The royalty and payment obligations in 4.2 can only be verified through the audit rights in section 5, but section 5 is a bare heading with no content.
suggested_fix: Add audit text giving Smith the right to inspect TDA's sales records on reasonable notice.

rationale: The indemnity in 13.3 makes Franchisee liable for all losses from operation of the restaurant, with only a gross-negligence carve-out for BKC, while 5.16.3 disclaims BKC responsibility for supply and cost of goods, so the franchisee bears risks that arise from BKC-system supply.
suggested_fix: Exclude from the 13.3 indemnity losses caused by BKC's negligence, breach, or its mandated supply arrangements.

rationale: Clause 5.6 bases Promotion Fees on Prescriber Data supplied by MBRK while 6.4 puts the cost of obtaining and reporting that data on MBRK, so DD's fee basis is in MBRK's hands with no verification mechanism.
suggested_fix: Give DD a right to audit and dispute the Prescriber Data used to calculate Promotion Fees.

rationale: The monthly Promotion Fee formula in 5.3 relies on Prescriber Data that 6.4 requires MBRK to obtain and report, so the fee calculation depends on MBRK's data function.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer 6.4 to 5.3 and require delivery of data by a fixed date each month.

rationale: Clause A's branding and product rights and Clause B's split of exclusive channels (TL's 'General Market' versus Integrity's 'direct mail ... e-commerce') leave overlapping, undefined channel boundaries such as Internet and e-commerce for each party.
suggested_fix: Define 'General Market' and 'Christian' e-commerce channels precisely and add a tie-break rule for sales that fall in both channels.

rationale: Clause A prices units sold to TL with a built-in copyright royalty while Clause B separately charges TL a per-unit royalty to Integrity on products sold, so royalty-type payments are duplicated or unclear.
suggested_fix: State expressly that the Clause 5 per-unit royalty is in addition to, and distinct from, the copyright and master-lease royalty included in the Clause 3 transfer price.

rationale: unreadable
Clause 11.1.1 is expressly made subject to Company's obligations under 11.1.2, which carries the actual tax collection, payment and indemnity.
Clause 6.8 relies on 'Force Majeure as defined in Section 2.2', so its excusal works only through that definition, and its interaction with termination rights is unclear.
suggested_fix: Add that a Force Majeure event exceeding a stated period entitles either party to terminate under Section 4 without liability.

rationale: Clause 15.6 termination rights and clause 3.1's ten-year term depend on each other, since the term runs 'unless previously terminated in accordance with Clause 15'.

Clause 15.3.2 requires each party to cease using the other's IP on termination, while clause 7.4 contemplates SHBV continuing as subcontractor under the Manufacturing Agreement, leaving unclear what happens to ongoing customer projects on termination.
suggested_fix: Add that termination does not affect obligations under any Manufacturing Agreement or W2E Customer contract already entered into.

rationale: Clause A binds 'successors and assigns' while B's warranties are personal to 'each party' and its 'right, title, interest and authority', leaving unclear whether warranties and the direct-damages-only limit pass to assignees.
suggested_fix: Add that successors and assigns take subject to the warranties and limitations of liability in Section 6 and that assignment requires prior written consent.

rationale: Section 9.1 gives eBix ownership of About Customer data and says it may freely disclose 'About Customer Data, as defined in Section 1', while also barring disclosure of 'About User data', a term undefined in the Section 1 definitions, so the restriction and the permission collide.
suggested_fix: Define 'About User data' consistently with 'About Customer Data' and state expressly which data eBix may disclose and which it may not, subject to applicable data protection law.

rationale: The non-exclusive, non-assignable licence in 1.1.1 only works if Party A's 5.1 warranties (truncated here) confirm it owns or can license the IP in the PRC.
suggested_fix: Complete clause 5.1 so Party A warrants it owns or is authorised to license the Intellectual Property in the PRC.

rationale: The restriction on sub-licensing in 1.2.1 depends on Party A's warranty in 5.1.4 of 'copyright or license', which is vague on whether Party A may license onward at all.
suggested_fix: Reword 5.1.4 to warrant that Party A owns the IP or holds rights sufficient to grant the licence in Clause 1.

rationale: Section 7.2 makes Distributor 'solely liable' for refunds on termination, which affects the fees and royalties payable under Section 6, whose body is absent here.
suggested_fix: State in Section 6 how refunds issued under Section 7.2 are treated against royalties payable to IMNTV.

rationale: Section 6.2(b) pays the last royalty after 'termination or expiration' while 7.1 allows termination on 30 days' uncured breach, without addressing set-off or withholding of royalties on breach.
suggested_fix: Add that the last payment under 6.2(b) is payable on termination under 7.1 subject to any amounts lawfully set off.

rationale: Pricing is 'TBD subject to Carrier's pricing policy' and revenue sharing starts October 1, 2005, so the termination clause cannot be applied against fixed commercial terms and the free pilot has no stated end.
suggested_fix: Fix the pilot end date and the revenue share formula in writing and state the consequences of termination during the pilot.

rationale: Exact's compliance warranty in 5.2(b)-(c) on the Anti-Kickback Statute and anti-corruption duplicates the mutual covenant in 5.4(b), with differing qualifiers ('material adverse effect' versus 'material compliance').
suggested_fix: Align the materiality qualifiers in 5.2 and 5.4 and state that 5.4 governs in case of inconsistency.

rationale: The Section 10 indemnity covers 'any violation of the Company's agreements, representations or warranties', so it depends on the Section 3 warranties, and 3(a) concedes Section 10 may be unenforceable as against public policy.
The Company's Section 6 covenants on effectiveness and stop orders feed the Section 9 closing conditions, which require the Registration Statement to be effective with no stop order.

Section 2 says that on failure to sell the minimum Shares the parties have no obligations except under Sections 2, 8, 10 and 11, so Section 8 expense payment obligations survive termination, and the $5,000 cap on Agent expenses is subject to Company consent.

Clause 14 has MMI indemnify Dragon Systems for loss or damage to its property, which duplicates the uncapped indemnity in Clause 7 for liabilities 'directly or indirectly' resulting from MMI's activities, and Clause 8 limits only MMI's consequential damages.
suggested_fix: State that the Clause 14 property indemnity falls under Clause 7 and that Clause 8 limits apply to both, with a monetary cap.

rationale: Clause A lets both parties terminate immediately on 'change of key management or control' and lets only Dragon terminate on 60 days' notice without cause, while B's set-off right lets Dragon deduct amounts owed by MMI's affiliates, so a termination dispute can interact with unsettled payments.
suggested_fix: Make the no-cause termination right mutual and state that accrued payment and set-off rights survive termination.

rationale: The indemnity in Section 6(a)(i) covers losses from 'any action taken by the Agent... as described in Section 2', so its scope depends on the services defined in Section 2.
suggested_fix: Limit the Section 6(a)(i) indemnity to actions within the scope of Section 2 and exclude the Agent's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

rationale: Section 7 contribution applies only where the Section 6 indemnity is 'held to be unenforceable', so it depends on Section 6, and Section 9 termination does not say whether Section 7 survives.
suggested_fix: Add that Sections 6 and 7 survive termination under Section 9.

rationale: The Section 8 indemnity for untrue statements depends on the accuracy of the Section 4 representations and warranties about the Registration Statement.
suggested_fix: Expressly state that the Section 8 indemnity operates for breach of the Section 4 representations and warranties.

rationale: Section 11 termination consequences cross-refer to Sections 2(a), 6, 8 and 9, and Section 6's expense and fee reimbursement duplicates the same expense payments, which risks inconsistency.
suggested_fix: Consolidate expense reimbursement in one section and have Section 11 refer to it only by reference.

rationale: Section 9.6 return of Confidential Information is triggered only by expiration, mutual termination or termination of Manufacturer's rights under Section 8, so it leaves unclear what happens on other terminations such as automatic termination under 8.3.
suggested_fix: Apply Section 9.6 on any expiration or termination of the Agreement under Section 8, however arising.

rationale: Exclusivity under Section 2 is conditional on the $52,000,000 Guaranteed Minimum, and AEIS's right to terminate or revoke exclusivity interacts with the assignment and modification rules in Section 3, which let AEIS assign freely but restrict Seller.
suggested_fix: State that any assignment by AEIS binds the assignee to the exclusivity and Marketing Rights Fee terms.

rationale: Clause A leaves the Manufacturing Agreement 'to be entered into' and clause B's 'intention' wording that W2E is prime contractor with SHBV as subcontractor is non-binding, leaving responsibilities unclear.
suggested_fix: Replace 'it is the intention' with 'W2E shall be the prime contractor and SHBV shall act as subcontractor under the executed Manufacturing Agreement'.

rationale: Section 8.1 says each party owns its own technology and Biocept owns improvements 'generated during the performance', while 8.3 allocates Developments by inventorship, so ownership of improvements may be determined by two different rules.
suggested_fix: State in 8.3 that Biocept's CEE/Selector improvements under 8.1 prevail over the inventorship-based ownership rule.

rationale: Section 8.4 makes allocation of third-party licence expenses 'subject to Section 8.5', which separately fixes who bears costs for Phase I versus Phase II and CTC-related licences, so 8.4 works only through 8.5.
suggested_fix: Align the Phase I/II and CTC cost-allocation wording in 8.4 and 8.5 and add a fallback if good-faith negotiation fails.

rationale: unreadable

Servicer's fees under Section 3.8 are payable only while the agreement subsists, and Section 8.3 ends the agreement on the last Receivable being paid or the Issuer's termination, without stating survival of accrued fees.
suggested_fix: Add that accrued and unpaid Servicing Fees survive termination under Section 8.3.

rationale: Section 5 relieves the Company of premiums after termination 'in accordance with Section 11', which itself terminates only on the Trust's repayment of premiums paid, so the premium obligation depends on that trigger.
suggested_fix: State that the Company's premium obligation continues until the Section 11 repayment is actually received by the Company.

rationale: Section 18(b) lets each party assign freely on a merger or sale, while Section 9(c) names MBE the 'exclusive retail shipping partner' of the Company, so an assignee could undo that exclusivity.
suggested_fix: Make assignment on change of control subject to the assignee's assumption of the exclusivity obligations in Section 9(c) or to the other party's consent.

rationale: Section 10(a) limits disclosure to employees, consultants, contractors or agents with a need to know, while 10(b) only requires 'reasonable efforts' not to disclose and 18(b) permits assignment on merger, so the standard of protection and who may receive information differ.
suggested_fix: Align 10(a) and 10(b) to a single standard and require assignees under 18(b) to be bound by equivalent confidentiality obligations.

rationale: Clause 12.1 requires signed written amendments but carves out Channel Notification Documents, whose unilateral price and product changes defined in 2.1 therefore operate as amendments without the counterparty's signature.
suggested_fix: Specify in 12.1 that Channel Notification Documents may change only prices and product information and take effect on stated prior written notice to Resellers.

rationale: Section 3 makes release of funds on the Closing Date conditional on compliance with Section 8 conditions to the Agent's satisfaction, so the closing mechanics only work through Section 8.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer expressly to the Section 8 conditions and specify the consequence if they are not satisfied by the Closing Date.

rationale: Section 10 contribution operates only where Section 9 indemnification is unavailable and allocates by the Section 2 fee percentage, so it depends on both other sections.
suggested_fix: State clearly that the Section 2 fee ratio uses fees actually paid and confirm the contribution applies only to the extent Section 9 is unenforceable.

rationale: On automatic termination under 6.5 the agreement is of no effect except Section 6.7, so the 7-day tax reimbursement duty in 10.1 is not clearly preserved for taxes paid before termination.
suggested_fix: Add that accrued payment obligations, including Section 10.1 tax reimbursements, survive termination under Section 6.5.

rationale: The mutual mark licence in 2.03 runs for the Term, but the assignment clause 9.09 lets PrimeCall assign to affiliates or on merger, so the mark licence may pass to a new party without DeltaThree's quality control.
suggested_fix: Provide that any assignee takes the mark licence subject to the owner's quality standards and that the licence is not otherwise transferable.

rationale: The Required Capital Contributions definition capped at $5,000,000 is operationalised by Section 2, which triggers contributions by reference to Schedule 10.28 compliance and repeats the cap.

Event of Default (d) depends on the $5,000,000 minimum committed capital test, which Section 20 evidences by affidavit on the Agent's request, so the default turns on evidence mechanics defined elsewhere.
suggested_fix: Specify a deadline for delivery of the Section 20 evidence and state that failure to deliver it is or is not itself a default under Section 10.

rationale: Termination under Section 21(ii) occurs on the Release Date defined in Section 19, which depends on the conditions there being met, and the reinstatement proviso may revive obligations after release.
suggested_fix: Clarify that the reinstatement proviso in Section 21 does not apply after a release under Section 19.

rationale: Section 15 selects Minnesota law while Section 16 gives the Agent an option to enforce in Minnesota courts, an asymmetric forum clause that does not provide arbitration.
suggested_fix: Make the jurisdiction clause mutual or provide for arbitration seated in a neutral place under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

rationale: The definition of "Confidential Information" in Section 1.1 only works through the cross-reference to Section 9.2, and "Foundational Software" through Section 5.4(a), so the meaning of the IP terms depends on those clauses.
suggested_fix: Verify that each cross-reference in Section 1.1 points to the correct operative section and that the Steam Book carve-out in Section 2.8 is expressly excluded from the general Intellectual Property allocation.

rationale: Developer's trademark rights under 6.1 exist only through individual Franchise Agreements, while 8.1 makes the whole Agreement freely assignable by El Pollo Loco, so what Developer holds depends on how assignment affects those Franchise Agreements.
suggested_fix: Add that any assignee by El Pollo Loco must assume all obligations and honour Developer's rights under this Agreement and the Franchise Agreements.

rationale: Section 6.1 confines Developer's use of the Marks to the Franchise Agreements, while 8.2 treats any stock sale or merger of Developer as a prohibited transfer and allows only mirrored-ownership entities as Franchisee, so both govern who may exercise the Marks.
suggested_fix: State expressly that permitted mirrored-ownership Franchisee entities may use the Marks under 6.1 and that consent under 8.2 is not to be unreasonably withheld.

rationale: Section 2.3 declares the Agreement void on expiry under 2.1 yet lists only Sections 2.2, 2.3, 3.1 and 3.9 as surviving, so obligations such as confidentiality and announcement (3.11) and any extension negotiation depend on this survival list.
suggested_fix: Add Section 3.11 and any other continuing obligations to the survival list in Section 2.3.

rationale: Section 3.9 bars disclosure until a public announcement is made under Section 3.11, so the confidentiality duty in 3.9 lapses or changes depending on the announcement mechanism and its legal-disclosure exception in 3.11.
suggested_fix: Clarify that after an announcement under 3.11 the confidentiality duty in 3.9 continues for non-public details of the Agreement.

rationale: Section 2.3 makes Section 3.9 survive termination, but 3.9 only restricts disclosure until an announcement under 3.11, which is not listed as surviving, leaving unclear how long the confidentiality duty lasts.
suggested_fix: Add Section 3.11 to the surviving provisions and state a fixed post-termination confidentiality period.

rationale: Survival clause 12.12 lists Sections 6.2, 9 and 10 as surviving, and Section 9.5's duty to stop using the trademarks on termination operates through that survival, with an inventory sell-off exception.
suggested_fix: State in Section 9.5 a fixed sell-off period for the Distributor's inventory after termination and confirm that it survives.

rationale: Section 26 Nonpetition Covenant applies 'notwithstanding any prior termination' and is listed in the table of contents/agreement frame, so it survives termination and works only through the termination provisions.
suggested_fix: Add an express survival clause listing Section 26 as surviving termination until one year and one day after payment in full of the VRRM-MFP Shares.

rationale: Section 11(a) exculpates the Remarketing Agent except for bad faith, gross negligence or wilful misconduct while Section 9(a) has the Fund and Adviser indemnify it for losses including breach of obligations, so the liability standard and indemnity scope are not aligned.
suggested_fix: State that the indemnity in Section 9 does not extend to losses arising from the Remarketing Agent's bad faith, gross negligence or wilful misconduct, consistently with Section 11(a).

rationale: Section 5 preserves payment for completed Services and says Section 2 survives termination, while Section 2 allows unilateral compensation adjustment on 14 days' notice and Section 5 allows termination on notice of unspecified length, so the surviving rate depends on cross-referenced terms.
suggested_fix: Specify a minimum termination notice period and provide that fees for services performed are payable at the rate in force when performed.

rationale: The survival clause expressly lists Section 5.2 (Invoicing) as surviving, and Section 5.2 itself contains post-termination true-up mechanics, so the two operate together.
unreadable
Force majeure excuses 'failure to perform' without carving out payment obligations, leaving unclear whether the Section 4.6 quarterly revenue-share payment can be suspended.
suggested_fix: Add that force majeure does not excuse payment obligations accrued under Section 4.6.

rationale: Section 3.7 payment within the stated days is excused only where Vapotherm has rejected the shipment under Section 4.2, so payment depends on the rejection conditions, which set no notice period.
suggested_fix: Specify a fixed period within which Vapotherm must give rejection notice under Section 4.2, failing which the shipment is deemed accepted and invoiced.

rationale: Section 2.1(a) requires a firm PO for a rolling period of months while Section 3.2(b) requires ordering at least a stated percentage of the Final Forecast Quantity, two overlapping commitment mechanisms that may diverge.
suggested_fix: Consolidate the firm-order commitment into Section 3.2(b) and cross-refer to it from Section 2.1(a).

rationale: Section 14.4 refers to mediation 'before resorting to arbitration' but no arbitration agreement is shown and Section 14.3 only picks New York law, leaving the final forum unclear.
suggested_fix: State expressly that unresolved disputes after mediation shall be finally resolved by arbitration under specified rules, with seat and language.

rationale: The Term clause ends the agreement on October 31, 2010 'unless renewed by agreement or sooner terminated', but the termination clause's consequential-damages waiver 'upon termination' does not say whether it applies on natural expiry, and the stray race-vehicle services text leaves the scope of the work unclear.
suggested_fix: Provide that the waiver of consequential damages applies on expiry or termination, and move the race-vehicle services into a separate scope-of-services clause.

rationale: The termination clause's 'upon termination' consequences operate against the Torvec sponsorship benefits and the differential units supplied, which carry no stated payment schedule, so the payment heading is empty and the 'Payment Schedule' remains undefined.
suggested_fix: Add an express payment schedule and state which sponsorship benefits and equipment return obligations continue on termination.

rationale: Section 13 ends all use of Manning Identification and bars similar marks after the Contract Period, while the royalty under Section 4 and sell-off rights are tied to shipments, so the cut-off interacts with royalties on post-termination shipments and is a post-term restraint.
suggested_fix: Make Section 13 expressly subject to the sell-off in Section 14 and limit the post-term ban on similar marks to what is reasonably necessary to protect the licensed identification.

rationale: The post-termination sell-off in Section 14 depends on Section 4's royalty rates ('royalty at the rates specified herein'), but it uses monthly payment against Section 4's quarterly cycle.
suggested_fix: State that Section 14 monthly payments override the quarterly reporting cycle in Section 4(a) for the sell-off period.

rationale: Section 13.2 lists Sections 6, 9, 10 and 15 as surviving termination, and survival operates through the cross-referenced sections, which in the other clause include a warranty disclaimer and consequential damages exclusion.
suggested_fix: Confirm the cross-referenced section numbers, and state expressly whether the Section 8 warranty disclaimer survives termination.

rationale: Sabco's services clause covers show car and transporter provision bearing Prolong identification, and the show car clause separately fixes free days and a discounted rate, so the two duplicate the show-car terms.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer in Section 2.B to Section 5 as the sole provision governing show-car appearances and charges.

rationale: Section 6.2 allows termination of a Service for convenience on 30 days' notice, while Section 6.3 terminates the Agreement only when the Termination Date has occurred for all Services, so the partial and whole termination mechanics overlap and the cost pass-through is unclear.
suggested_fix: State that termination of the last remaining Service under Section 6.2 also triggers Section 6.3 and that Section 6.2(b) cost pass-through survives.

rationale: Wade's non-compete clause covers endorsements of Innerwear only during the Term, which depends on the scope of Naked's exclusive licence of the Wade Image for Naked Products, and the confidentiality agreement is left to a form 'mutually acceptable' and not yet defined.
suggested_fix: Attach the agreed form of non-disclosure agreement and align the non-compete scope to the licensed Territory and product category.

rationale: The termination clause's seven-day cure, ten-day notice and warrant forfeiture work through the four-year Term and Sell-off Period in Section 2, which only apply if Wade did not terminate, so the post-termination rights depend on how the term clause is read.
suggested_fix: State expressly how the Sell-off Period and exclusive negotiation right in Section 2 interact with termination by either party under Section 12.

rationale: Section 4.6 keeps Section 5 in effect after termination, so the Section 5.2 non-use and non-disclosure obligation survives only through that cross-reference, with no stated duration.
suggested_fix: Add a fixed confidentiality period, such as five years after termination, with trade secrets protected for as long as they remain secret.

rationale: Section 2.7 requires records to be kept for three years after expiration or termination, and Section 4.2 lets Anixa terminate without cause on 30 days' notice, so the records, inspection and confidentiality duties continue after termination only if the survival clause covers them.
suggested_fix: Add that the records retention and inspection obligations in Section 2.7 survive termination under Section 4.2.
